players.product: NeoFuse OTP and PUF-based security IP

quarterly_data.signal: Tape-outs and revenue by technology (revenue includes both licensing and royalty), 2025: NeoBit 253 new tape-outs and US$27,312,244; NeoFuse 248 and US$78,122,682; PUF-based 54 and US$7,645,293. Cumulative totals: NeoBit 5,382 tape-outs and US$482,412,457; NeoFuse 1,730 and US$384,164,465; PUF-based 160 and US$23,383,735.

Security business development (deck): eMemory provides security IPs through technology licensing and co-marketing with foundry platforms (TSMC, Intel, UMC, GF, etc.); works with CPU partners (Arm, RISC-V, Cadence, etc.) on pre-integrated CPU and security subsystems for SoC customers; and works with cloud service providers (Microsoft, Meta, Google, Amazon, etc.) on chip-level embedded security requirements, developing root-of-trust solutions for systems like AWS, Meta and Azure. Company claims: its RoT IP is fully ready to meet the hardware security requirements of the Caliptra specification; PUFPQC attains full NIST coverage; PUFtrng delivers 100x faster performance than a conventional TRNG.

Product positioning (company comparison): for a 32K x 8 density, one NeoFuse OTP macro of 0.33 mm2 replaces 16 e-Fuse macros of ~1.92 mm2 (>80% area reduction, no buffer SRAM required); SRAM repair needs 16~256Kb OTP. NeoFuse OTP provides an interface to Siemens Tessent MBIST (new MBISR: Tessent MBISR + NeoFuse), and the deck cites an Arm RSS (Runtime Security Subsystem) endorsement. For AI memory systems the deck lists OTP repair for SRAM/HBM/DRAM production yield and MTP configuration for DDR5/SOCAMM DIMMs.
quarterly_data.figure: 0.33 mm2 vs ~1.92 mm2 (>80% area reduction) at 32K x 8

connects_to.relationship: embedded NVM / security IP on TSMC processes
